title: Undecidable projection costs for quantum channels with finite tracial ancillas
abstract: We transfer a quantitative unitary-relation construction to a quadratic optimization problem for quantum channels. The input is a real rational orthogonal projection on the Choi space, together with an explicit rational bistochastic Choi state supported exactly on its kernel. The minimum cost over all bistochastic channels is therefore zero. Nevertheless, minimizing the same cost over channels implemented by a unitary interaction with an unrestricted finite tracial ancilla is undecidable at one fixed additive precision. The objective is a projective measurement probability, not a determinant. Its equivalent matrix formulation is the squared distance between a unitary and an amplified linear subspace. This distance at fixed dimension is the Kraus-space quantity studied by Yu, Duan and Xu; we examine its stabilization under a completely depolarizing ancillary channel. We prove the transfer with explicit constants, derive the absence of a recursive uniform ancilla bound, and give the exact answer when the subspace projection is completely positive. The source hardness and the relation compiler are inherited results; no general novelty claim about noncomputable tracial optimization is made.
